**Yes.** Hansen Global Forest Change data detected 1.8 hectares of tree-cover loss on the property in 2019, about 0.05% of its area. The 2021 national forest map classifies the affected area as planted pine forest, not native forest.

A further 3.1 hectares of loss was detected in patches smaller than 0.5 hectares; these were not counted as an event under the tool’s threshold.

The JRC map classified the entire 1.8-hectare event area as forest in 2020. This does not by itself establish the cause of the loss or whether it was permanent.
